post.caption: A girl found it in rubble. In the early 1980s in Mbuji Mayi, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a young girl playing in rubble near her uncle's house found a rough diamond of 890 carats. The rubble was mine waste. Master cutter Marvin Samuels spent about four years on the Incomparable, chose clarity over size, and made a 407 carat stone that was fancy brownish yellow and internally flawless. He called its triangular shape a triolette. Fourteen smaller gems were cut beside it. Later it was recut into the 303 carat Golden Canary.
